prompt:
Bug report: with the `toc` extension, a heading like `# Hello world !` gets the id `hello-world-`, with a trailing dash. Fix it and add a regression test.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Fixed: `# Hello world !` with `toc` now gets the id `hello-world`. `slugify` in `markdown/extensions/toc.py` now strips surrounding whitespace left behind after punctuation is removed, before whitespace is turned into separators; this also fixes the leading case (`# ! Hello world` gave `-hello-world`). I added two regression tests (trailing and leading punctuation) and an Unreleased changelog entry; the full suite passes, and both new tests fail without the fix. Not changed: a heading that ends in a literal hyphen (`# Hello -`) still yields `hello-`, since hyphens in the heading text are kept deliberately.
